title: Agentforce concepts, topics, instructions, actions, grounding, and channels
objectives: Explain an Agentforce agent as a goal-oriented application assembled from subagents (formerly topics), instructions, actions, grounding, and channels.
State that beginning April 2026 Help calls agent topics subagents, with no functionality change.
Separate instructions (natural-language standing orders) from actions (what the agent can invoke) and from grounding (where answers come from).
Refuse invented edition or SKU gates; mark them Needs verification unless Help cites them.
diagnostic_question: A service VP wants a 24/7 chat that answers shipping FAQs from Knowledge, can create a Case, and escalates refund fights to a human. Which parts are a subagent (formerly a topic), which are instructions, which are actions, which are grounding, and which is the channel?
definition: An Agentforce agent is a goal-oriented, autonomous AI application that converses, chooses jobs, and completes a sequence of tasks using business data. Help currently calls those jobs subagents; they were named agent topics before April 2026, with no functionality change. Each subagent is shaped by instructions, enabled actions, grounding data, and the channel where the conversation runs. ([Design and Implement Agents](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_intro.htm); [Get to Know Agentforce Service Agent](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.bots_service_asa_about.htm); [Subagents](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_topics_parent.htm))
why_it_matters: Interviewers still say Copilot topics. Mixing a channel, a Knowledge article, a Flow action, and a paragraph of instructions into one blob produces the wrong Builder screen, the wrong test, and the wrong risk review. Help renamed Einstein Copilot for Salesforce to Agentforce and agent topics to subagents; the building blocks did not merge into one product.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of a restaurant kitchen brigade. The Agentforce agent is the head chef who talks to the dining room. Each station is a subagent—formerly called a topic—with a job such as shipping FAQ or refunds. The station recipe card is instructions. The burners, tickets, and POS buttons are actions. The pantry of approved ingredients is grounding. The dining room, pass-through window, or room-service phone is the channel. Einstein Trust Layer is the health-code camera, not a station.
deeper_explanation: Salesforce Help describes Agentforce as the agent-driven layer of the Salesforce Platform: tools to create and customize agents for sales, service, marketing, commerce, Slack, and more. An agent is not a single prompt; it is assembled from jobs, actions, data, and a place to talk. ([Design and Implement Agents](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_intro.htm))

Help defines AI agents as goal-oriented, autonomous applications that can initiate and complete a sequence of tasks, handle natural language, and securely provide answers drawn from business data. Agentforce Service Agent (ASA) is the service-specialized type that can work messaging channels and transfer complex or sensitive conversations to live reps. ([Get to Know Agentforce Service Agent](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.bots_service_asa_about.htm))

Beginning April 2026, Help calls agent topics subagents, with no functionality change. A subagent is a particular job an agent can do. Teach the current name, and mention topics only as the former name so a whiteboard that still says topics does not fail. ([Subagents](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_topics_parent.htm); [Design and Implement Agents](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_intro.htm))

Subagents (formerly topics) exist so the agent selects a relevant job instead of choosing from one flat list of every action. Each subagent bundles instructions and the actions allowed for that job. ([Subagents](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_topics_parent.htm))

Instructions are natural-language standing orders for how that job should behave. Actions are the invocable work—standard agent actions, flows, Apex, prompt templates—the agent is allowed to run. Grounding is how answers are retrieved from allowed data such as an Agentforce Data Library (vector store, search index, retriever). Channels are where the conversation is offered. Configure agents in Agentforce Builder or Agentforce Studio; Prompt Builder is a separate workshop for reusable templates. ([Get to Know Agentforce Service Agent](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.bots_service_asa_about.htm))

Agentforce Service Agent (ASA) can work messaging channels including Enhanced Chat, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, LINE, Apple Messages for Business, SMS, and Bring Your Own Channel (BYOC), with Omni-Channel flows for routing and human transfer. IT Service Agent templates currently do not support Email, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, or Web Chat—verify channel fit before promising a template. ([Get to Know Agentforce Service Agent](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.bots_service_asa_about.htm); [Set Up Agentforce](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.it_srvcs_agentforce_setup.htm))

Name hygiene: Einstein Copilot for Salesforce is now Agentforce; topics are now subagents; Data Cloud is now Data 360. Help documents up to 20 versions of a single agent and one active version of Agentforce (Default). Exact add-on SKUs vary by agent type and remain Needs verification unless a cited Help edition table covers the org. ([Einstein Copilot for Salesforce is Now Agentforce](https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=release-notes.rn_einstein_copilot.htm))

mental_model.analogy: A restaurant kitchen brigade on a Saturday night: one chef coordinates stations, each station has a recipe card, tools, a walk-in of mise en place, and a window to the dining room.
useful_mapping: Agentforce agent → chef de cuisine who converses and sequences jobs
subagent (formerly topic) → a station with one job (grill vs pastry)
instructions → the station recipe card and standing orders
actions → burners, tickets, and POS buttons the station may use
grounding / Agentforce Data Library → pantry of approved ingredients
channel → dining room, pass window, or room-service phone
human transfer → sending a dish back to the floor manager
Einstein Trust Layer → health-code cameras, not a station
where_it_breaks: A brigade is people with employment law; an agent is licensed software with grounding and actions.
One station recipe cannot replace an action that must write a Case.
Einstein Bots still exist in Help; ASA is not a rename of Einstein Bots.
The analogy does not encode Einstein Requests, Flex Credits, or edition add-ons.

teach_back_prompt: Without using Copilot as a current product name, walk a service manager through subagents (formerly topics), instructions, actions, grounding, and channels using the kitchen-brigade mapping, then name one place the analogy breaks.

review_schedule.prompt: From memory: subagent vs former topic name, plus instructions vs actions vs grounding vs channel.
Given FAQ chat, Case-create, and WhatsApp, assign each building block.
Explain why a long instruction is not a substitute for an action or a Data Library.
Correct a slide that still says Einstein Copilot topics in Data Cloud.
Two-minute interview: assemble an ASA-style agent from the five building blocks.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: An Agentforce agent is assembled from subagents—formerly topics—plus instructions, actions, grounding, and a channel. Instructions are standing orders. Actions do work. Grounding retrieves allowed data. The channel is where the user talks. Copilot is the former name.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I start with the job, not the LLM. Help calls that job a subagent; older slides say topic. I write instructions as natural-language guardrails for that job, then I attach only the actions the job is allowed to run. If the answer must come from Knowledge or files, I configure grounding rather than stuffing articles into the instruction text. Then I pick the channel and a human-transfer path, especially for ASA. I correct Copilot to Agentforce. SKUs stay Needs verification.

terminology.plain: An AI worker on Salesforce that can talk and complete a sequence of jobs inside guardrails.
terminology.precise: Help: goal-oriented, autonomous AI applications that perform tasks and business interactions, handle natural language, and draw answers from business data.
terminology.example: Agentforce Service Agent answering a shipping question on Enhanced Chat, then escalating a refund fight.
terminology.non_example: A scheduled Flow that stamps Status every night with no conversation.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Prompt template: one generation call, not the agent's job catalog.
terminology.boundary: Prompt Builder template types are AI-003; this lesson only names templates as an action source.

terminology.plain: One job the agent is allowed to do, with its own instructions and actions.
terminology.precise: Help: beginning April 2026, agent topics are called subagents; no functionality change. A subagent is a particular job an agent can do.
terminology.example: A Refund Request subagent with instructions and a create-case action.
terminology.non_example: A Chatter topic on a record feed, or a Knowledge data category used as if it were an agent job.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Prompt template: LLM instructions for one generation, not the agent's job catalog.
terminology.boundary: Do not teach topic as the current Help name except as an alias.

terminology.plain: Natural-language standing orders for how that job should behave.
terminology.precise: Builder-authored guidance that steers the agent for a subagent: tone, what to ask, when to refuse, when to escalate. Not a substitute for an invocable action.
terminology.example: Never promise a refund amount; transfer billing disputes to a human.
terminology.non_example: A Flow that actually issues the refund.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Prompt template instructions in Prompt Builder: those are for one generation call, not the agent's job catalog.
terminology.boundary: Trust and human approval depth is AI-005.

terminology.plain: The work the agent is allowed to invoke: standard actions, flows, Apex, prompt templates.
terminology.precise: Help ties agents to completing a sequence of tasks; those tasks are represented as actions the agent may select. Exact action catalog is org- and type-dependent.
terminology.example: Answer Questions with Knowledge; a Flow that creates a LAB_ Case.
terminology.non_example: A paragraph in instructions that pretends the Case already exists.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Flow run from a button: deterministic automation, not an agent choosing among actions.
terminology.boundary: Choosing Flow versus an agent is AI-007.

terminology.plain: Retrieving allowed company data so answers are based on your records, not the model's memory.
terminology.precise: ASA Help describes Agentforce Data Library as simplifying RAG: vector store, search index, and retriever so agents can search, retrieve, and ground responses.
terminology.example: A Data Library over LAB_ Shipping FAQ Knowledge articles.
terminology.non_example: Pasting a policy PDF into the instruction field and calling it grounding.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Sharing rules: who may see a record is not the same as what the retriever indexed.

terminology.plain: The surface where the user talks to the agent.
terminology.precise: Help places agents on Lightning, Slack, messaging, and other supported surfaces depending on agent type. ASA specializes in service messaging channels.
terminology.example: Enhanced Chat / Messaging for In-App and Web for ASA.
terminology.non_example: A Field Generation template on a Lightning record page with no conversation.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Omni-Channel queue: routing to humans or agents, not the agent definition itself.
terminology.boundary: Exact channel setup clicks are Needs verification in the org Help for that channel.

terminology.plain: The service-specialized agent type that can chat with customers and hand off to a human.
terminology.precise: Help: a service agent type that can work messaging channels and transfer complex or sensitive conversations to live reps, similar in that handoff idea to Einstein Bots—but ASA is an AI agent type on Agentforce.
terminology.example: ASA on Enhanced Chat for shipping FAQs with Omni-Channel transfer for billing.
terminology.non_example: Calling every employee Lightning agent ASA.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Einstein Bots: related product; not the same metadata type in Help.
terminology.boundary: Employee agent / Agentforce (Default) is a different type in the Agentforce map.

terminology.plain: The Setup experience where you configure an agent's subagents, instructions, actions, grounding, and channels.
terminology.precise: Help refers to Agentforce Builder and Agentforce Studio as the agent configuration surfaces, distinct from Prompt Builder (templates) and from legacy builder labels that may still appear during transition.
terminology.example: Opening Agentforce Studio to add a Shipping FAQ subagent and attach a Data Library.
terminology.non_example: Authoring a Field Generation template in Prompt Builder.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Prompt Builder: template workshop, not the agent job catalog.
terminology.boundary: Exact Setup navigation and legacy vs Studio labels are Needs verification per org.

terminology.plain: The employee-facing agent in Lightning (and related employee surfaces), formerly Copilot.
terminology.precise: Help renamed Einstein Copilot for Salesforce to Agentforce. Setup may show Agentforce or Agentforce (Default) for the employee agent.
terminology.example: A seller asking the employee agent to summarize an Opportunity they already can see.
terminology.non_example: A customer on WhatsApp talking to ASA.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: ASA: customer service channel agent, not the default employee agent.
terminology.boundary: Do not teach Copilot as the current brand.

when_to_use: When you must assemble Agentforce concepts into a working agent: topics now called subagents, plus instructions, actions, grounding, and channels.
When a design review still says Einstein Copilot topics and you need to map those topics to current subagents without changing the job catalog.
When instructions are being used as a dumping ground and you must split standing orders from actions and from grounding.
When choosing a channel (Lightning, Slack, Enhanced Chat) and a human-transfer path for Agentforce Service Agent versus an employee agent.
when_not_to_use: Do not use this Agentforce concepts lesson as a substitute for Prompt Builder templates, inputs, outputs, and evaluation (AI-003).
Do not treat a paragraph of instructions as Data Cloud / Data 360 grounding and retrieval design (AI-004).
Do not use subagent cataloguing to skip Trust Layer permissions, data exposure, and human approval (AI-005).
Do not use this building-block map to choose deterministic automation versus an agent (AI-007), or to skip testing and versioning (AI-006).
configuration_or_code_location: Setup → Agentforce Agents / Agentforce Builder / Agentforce Studio (labels vary; legacy builder may still appear—Needs verification in the org).
Help: Design and Implement Agents (ai.copilot_intro.htm) and Subagents (ai.agent_topics_parent.htm).
Setup path for service agents: Set Up Agentforce (service.it_srvcs_agentforce_setup.htm).
Needs verification: leftover Topics labels versus Subagents in Builder.

Enhanced Chat as the requested channel

decisions.decision: Create two subagents (formerly topics): Shipping FAQ and Callback Request—not one mega-topic.
decisions.because: Help defines a subagent as a particular job an agent can do; mixing refund fights into shipping FAQ instructions hides the transfer rule.
decisions.rejected: One topic named Agentforce that does everything

decisions.decision: Ground Shipping FAQ with an Agentforce Data Library; do not paste articles into instructions.
decisions.because: ASA Help describes Data Library RAG for search, retrieve, and ground.

decisions.decision: Attach the callback Flow as an action; put refund transfer in instructions plus Omni-Channel/human handoff.
decisions.because: Actions complete tasks; instructions constrain; ASA Help supports transfer of complex or sensitive conversations.
decisions.rejected: Asking the LLM to 'just create a Case' with no action

configuration_or_code: Write a LAB_ brigade map: two stations, recipe cards, one Flow action, one Data Library, Enhanced Chat channel.

hands_on_lab.environment: Disposable Developer sandbox or scratch org; synthetic LAB_ records only. Skip enablement steps you are not licensed for.
starting_state_checks: You can open Salesforce Help in a browser.
You will not enable paid add-ons in production.
steps: Open Design and Implement Agents and copy the Agentforce definition plus the subagents rename sentence into LAB_notes.
Open the Subagents Help topic (ai.agent_topics_parent.htm) and write one sentence: a subagent is a particular job; topics is the former name.
Open Get to Know Agentforce Service Agent and list Prompt Builder, Data Library, channel, and human transfer as four separate boxes.
If Agentforce Builder is available, inspect whether the UI says Topics or Subagents and record the leftover as a transition note—do not change production agents.
guided_completion: If you cannot enable Agentforce, the lab is still complete: Help reading plus the written brigade map.
If Setup still shows Copilot or Topics, record it as a transition leftover.
hands_on_lab.independent_challenge: A VP says 'one Copilot topic for everything including refunds.' Rewrite into two subagents, instructions, one action, grounding, and a channel.
evidence: LAB_notes with four Help URLs and the topics→subagents alias.
A paste of the Help sentence you quoted, not a blog.
stop_recovery_cleanup: Delete LAB_notes from the sandbox if you created a record.
Do not leave production Agentforce enablement from this lab.
hands_on_lab.limitations: This lab does not provision Agentforce licenses.

decision_table.signal: The agent must handle a distinct job with its own actions and tone, and slides still say topic.
decision_table.choose: Model it as a subagent and mention topic only as the former Help name.
decision_table.not: A Chatter topic, a Knowledge category, or one mega-instruction block for every job.
decision_table.why: Help defines a subagent as a particular job an agent can do and renamed topics in April 2026.

decision_table.signal: You need the agent to create a record, call a Flow, or run a prompt template.
decision_table.choose: Attach an action; keep instructions as standing orders only.
decision_table.not: A longer instruction that pretends the write already happened.
decision_table.why: Help defines agents as completing a sequence of tasks; tasks map to actions, not prose.

decision_table.signal: Answers must come from Knowledge or uploaded files rather than model memory.
decision_table.choose: Configure grounding such as an Agentforce Data Library; defer RAG depth to AI-004.
decision_table.not: Pasting policy text into the subagent instructions and calling it grounded.
decision_table.why: ASA Help describes Data Library RAG: vector store, search index, retriever.

decision_table.signal: Stakeholders pick an IT Service Agent template and ask for Email or Web Chat on day one.
decision_table.choose: Verify channel support in Set Up Agentforce before promising Email, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, or Web Chat.
decision_table.not: Assuming every ASA channel works on every template, especially IT Service.
decision_table.why: IT Service Agent templates currently do not support Email, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, or Web Chat per Help.

decision_table.signal: Customers will talk on messaging and some utterances are sensitive or complex.
decision_table.choose: Deploy Agentforce Service Agent on a supported messaging channel with Omni-Channel human transfer.
decision_table.not: An employee Lightning agent as the customer WhatsApp or SMS strategy.
decision_table.why: ASA Help lists messaging channels and supports transferring complex or sensitive conversations to live reps.

limitations: Does not teach Prompt Builder template types in depth (AI-003).
Does not teach Data 360 retrieval index mechanics (AI-004).
Does not configure Testing Center or agent versions (AI-006).
Edition, add-on, and credit meters are Needs verification unless cited.
security_notes: Actions can write CRM data; least-privilege the action catalog.
Grounding is not a substitute for sharing; exposure is AI-005.
Do not claim data masking is on for every Agentforce type; Help says it can be disabled for some agents.
common_mistakes: Using Einstein Copilot as the current Salesforce agent name.
Teaching topic as the current Help name without the subagent alias.
Expecting instructions to create records without an action.
Stating edition gates that Help did not cite.

troubleshooting.symptom: The agent answers shipping questions with invented policy text.

troubleshooting.do_not_assume: A longer instruction will replace retrieval.

troubleshooting.symptom: The agent promises a Case but none is created.

Does the running user have permission to create that record?
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: The LLM can write Salesforce records by talking.

troubleshooting.symptom: A design doc says Copilot topics in Data Cloud.
check: Verify Builder labels in the org.
troubleshooting.do_not_assume: The org UI has finished every rename.

production_notes: Do not expose a customer channel without a human-transfer path for sensitive jobs.
Do not enable Agentforce in production from this lesson.
Reverify Help names on the org's release.

flashcards.front: What are agent topics called as of April 2026 Help?
flashcards.back: Subagents — same functionality, new name. Mention topics only as the former name.
A particular job an agent can do, with instructions and actions for that job.

flashcards.front: What is an AI agent in Help?
flashcards.back: A goal-oriented autonomous application that can complete a sequence of tasks, converse, and use business data.
Natural-language standing orders for a subagent: tone, refuse rules, when to escalate—not CRM writes.
Invocable work the agent may run: standard actions, flows, Apex, or prompt templates.

flashcards.front: What is grounding at this lesson's level?
flashcards.back: Retrieving allowed company data (for example Agentforce Data Library RAG) so answers are not invented.
The surface where the user talks: Lightning, Slack, Enhanced Chat, or another supported messaging surface.
A service-specialized agent type that can work messaging channels and transfer sensitive or complex chats to humans.

flashcards.front: What happened to Einstein Copilot for Salesforce?
flashcards.back: It was renamed to Agentforce. Do not teach Copilot as the current brand.

flashcards.front: Where are prompt templates managed that agents may call?
flashcards.back: Prompt Builder is where you create, test, and manage reusable prompt templates.
Instructions constrain; actions do work; grounding retrieves allowed data for answers.

flashcards.front: Are Einstein Bots identical to ASA?
flashcards.back: No. Help compares handoff behavior but defines ASA as an Agentforce AI agent type.
Employee / Agentforce (Default) helps internal users; ASA serves customers on service channels.

flashcards.front: How do you treat uncited edition gates?
flashcards.back: Mark Needs verification. Help says add-on licenses vary by agent type.
Builder configures the agent (subagents, actions, channels); Prompt Builder authors reusable templates.
Data 360 (rebrand dated 14 October 2025 in Help). Grounding depth is AI-004.

flashcards.front: Which messaging channels does ASA Help list?
flashcards.back: Enhanced Chat, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, LINE, Apple Messages for Business, SMS, and BYOC, with Omni-Channel routing.

flashcards.front: Which channels do IT Service Agent templates NOT support?
flashcards.back: Email, WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, and Web Chat—verify before promising those channels.

flashcards.front: How many agent versions does Help allow?
flashcards.back: Up to 20 versions of a single agent; one active version of Agentforce (Default).

interview_questions.question: Explain subagents, instructions, actions, grounding, and channels in plain English.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A subagent is one job—Help used to call it a topic. Instructions are standing orders. Actions are the Flow, Apex, or templates it may run. Grounding retrieves allowed data. The channel is where the user talks.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I assemble an Agentforce agent the way Help does, not as one prompt. Jobs are subagents (formerly topics). I write instructions as natural-language guardrails, then I attach only the actions that job is allowed to invoke. If answers must come from Knowledge or files, I configure grounding such as an Agentforce Data Library instead of pasting documents into instructions. Then I pick the channel and, for ASA, a human-transfer path. Copilot is a former name.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ Enhanced Chat: Shipping FAQ subagent grounded on Knowledge; Callback subagent with a Flow action; refunds transfer to a human.
weak_answer_warnings: Calling everything a topic as if that were still the current name
Using Copilot as the current product name

interview_questions.question: A hiring manager still says Einstein Copilot topics. What do you say?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Help renamed Einstein Copilot for Salesforce to Agentforce, and beginning April 2026 agent topics are called subagents with no functionality change. I use the current names and treat the old words as aliases.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not shame the interviewer. I map Copilot to Agentforce and topics to subagents, then I ask which job, which actions, which grounding, and which channel they meant. If their org UI still shows Topics, I call it a transition leftover and verify in Builder rather than arguing from a blog. Data Cloud on the same slide becomes Data 360 for grounding conversations.
interview_questions.example: A slide titled 'Copilot topics in Data Cloud' becomes Agentforce subagents grounded with Data 360 / Agentforce Data Library.
weak_answer_warnings: Inventing a third product called Copilot GPT

interview_questions.question: Service wants 24/7 chat that answers FAQs, opens callback Cases, and escalates billing fights. How do you split the building blocks?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Two or more subagents, not one blob. FAQ uses grounding. Callback uses an action. Billing uses instructions plus human transfer on an ASA messaging channel.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I refuse a single Copilot topic. Shipping FAQ is a subagent grounded on Knowledge via Data Library. Callback is a subagent whose action is the existing Flow. Refund-amount arguments are not an LLM math problem; ASA Help supports transferring complex or sensitive conversations to live reps. Enhanced Chat is the channel. Prompt templates, if any, live in Prompt Builder and are called as actions. SKUs stay Needs verification.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ org: ASA on Messaging for In-App and Web, two subagents, one Flow, one Data Library.
follow_ups: When do you refuse an action?
weak_answer_warnings: One instruction file replaces Flow and Knowledge

interview_questions.question: Why not put all Knowledge into instructions?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Instructions are standing orders, not a search index. Help points agents at Agentforce Data Library RAG—vector store, search index, retriever—so answers are retrieved, not stuffed.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: A pasted policy goes stale, blows past useful instruction length, and is not retrieval. Grounding is the data path; AI-004 owns index Ready status and retrievers. Instructions should say how to use retrieved answers and when to escalate. I also separate unauthorized facts (sharing, AI-005) from invented facts (hallucination).
interview_questions.example: LAB_ Shipping FAQ articles in a Data Library versus a 2,000-word instruction paste.
follow_ups: What if the index is not Ready?
weak_answer_warnings: The LLM remembers whatever we typed in Builder

interview_questions.question: Is Agentforce Service Agent just Einstein Bots?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: No. Help says ASA can transfer to live reps similar to Einstein Bots, but ASA is an AI agent type on Agentforce that uses subagents, Prompt Builder, and Data Libraries.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I respect that channel and Omni-Channel patterns look familiar to bot admins. I then quote the agent definition: goal-oriented, autonomous, sequence of tasks, natural language, answers from business data. The reasoning layer is now subagents (formerly topics), instructions, and actions. I do not tell a bot specialist their skills are useless; I tell them the catalog changed.
interview_questions.example: Existing Enhanced Chat that used a bot, now evaluated for ASA plus Omni-Channel flow routing.
tradeoffs: Reuse channel skills vs new reasoning model

interview_questions.question: What is Prompt Builder versus Agentforce Builder in this lesson?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Prompt Builder authors reusable prompt templates. Agentforce Builder or Studio is where you configure subagents, instructions, actions, grounding, and channels. Templates can be actions the agent calls.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Help is explicit that agents and other generative features use prompt templates managed in Prompt Builder. The agent still needs a job catalog, actions, grounding, and a channel. I do not configure an agent inside a Field Generation template, and I do not write a 40-line prompt in Builder hoping it replaces an action. Template types themselves are AI-003.
interview_questions.example: Field Generation template on LAB_ Case versus ASA using Answer Questions with Knowledge as an action.
weak_answer_warnings: Builder and Prompt Builder are the same Setup page

interview_questions.question: The agent never creates the callback Case. How do you debug the building blocks?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Check whether a Case-create action is attached to the subagent, whether the utterance classified to that job, and whether the running user can create the record. Do not add more instruction poetry first.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I walk the brigade. Did the channel deliver the utterance? Did the planner pick the Callback subagent rather than Shipping FAQ? Is the Flow action enabled and succeeding? Sharing and FLS can block the write even when the LLM sounds confident. Grounding will not create records. Testing and versioning are AI-006; I still refuse to ship a customer channel without seeing one successful action log.
interview_questions.example: LAB_ utterance 'please call me tomorrow' routes to Shipping FAQ because the callback subagent description is empty.
follow_ups: Where do you see action errors?
weak_answer_warnings: The model will create the Case if we ask nicely

interview_questions.question: When would you refuse to add another subagent?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: When the need is a deterministic formula, a single drafted field, or a score from history. Also when they cannot name grounding data, an action, or a human escalation path for a customer channel.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: AI-007 owns the full tool-choice table, but this lesson still needs judgment. Same-record math is Flow or a formula. A one-click summary field is generative via Prompt Builder. A nightly churn number is predictive. A subagent is justified when natural language plus a job plus actions plus a channel is the actual requirement. I also refuse a customer-facing job with no transfer path for sensitive utterances. Uncited SKUs stay Needs verification.
interview_questions.example: Request to 'AI-update Amount to Amount*1.1 on save'—that is Flow or a formula, not a new Agentforce topic/subagent.
follow_ups: What is a limitation of agents?
